articles.title: A Design Space Exploration of Async/Await
articles.summary: Many programming languages now provide the async/await keywords for expressing concurrency, but the design rationale is consistent: to make concurrent programs look more like straight-line code. This paradigm encompasses async/await as straight-line asynchrony, as opposed to using event loops or callbacks. Language designs for straight-line asynchrony have been brewing for over 15 years, and a design space exploration of async/await reveals a lot more different than expected. Modern languages diverge significantly, with seven different runtimes producing different outputs for a simple program, and the concept of "cold" or "hot" async function calls, or "Eagerness", is a design dimension that affects the observable semantics of program execution.
